hypothesis: CVaR-QAOA (alpha < 1) achieves a smaller median objective gap to the Track-A exact optimum than expectation-QAOA (alpha = 1) at matched circuit depth, consistent with Barkoutsos & Nannicini (2020).
benchmark_problem: Ladder n in [4,6,8,10] (revised down from the original [4..14] preregistration draft after discovering the exact slack-bit QUBO encoding needs more qubits than a penalty-only encoding at n>10 -- see QUANTUM1B_PREREGISTRATION.md 'Preregistration deviations'; n in [12,14] remain in EXP-A2/EXP-B3 which do not require full QAOA optimization), families [independent, correlated, tight_budget, degenerate, concentrated, conflicting_constraints], one instance per (family, n), seed 0 for instance generation
classical_comparator: EXP-A1's exact/MILP optimum on the identical OptionSelectionInstance (same qubo_encoding.build_qubo call)
quantum_method: NumPy statevector-exact QAOA (experiments.quantum1b.cvar_qaoa), both expectation and CVaR-alpha aggregation, COBYLA, maxiter=200
compute_budget: target < 4 hours wall-clock; if exceeded, reduce to p in [1,2], 3 seeds, n<=8, documented before re-running

pass_fail_interpretation.PROMISING_FOR_FURTHER_TESTING: CVaR-QAOA (best alpha) achieves median objective gap <= expectation-QAOA's median gap, difference significant at two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p<0.05 across (family,n) cells, AND feasible-probability >= 0.5 in the majority of cells
pass_fail_interpretation.RESEARCH_ONLY: directionally consistent but non-significant improvement, or works only on a subset of families
pass_fail_interpretation.NO_GO: no improvement, underperforms expectation-QAOA, or negligible feasible-probability across most cells

prohibited_conclusion: no claim of quantum advantage regardless of outcome -- compares two QAOA variants against the classical optimum only, never claims to beat classical solver runtime/resource cost
